usage.callShape: POST https://img402.dev/api/upload/token with empty JSON body {} (x402 paid, $0.01 USDC on Base)
usage.outputShape: body.token (single-use upload token), body.expiresAt (ISO 8601, token valid ~10 min)
quirks: This endpoint does NOT return a CDN URL. It mints a single-use upload token only.
Two-step flow: (1) pay this endpoint to get body.token; (2) upload the actual image bytes in a separate follow-up request using the token as the X-Upload-Token header to receive the public CDN URL.
Token is valid for only ~10 minutes (body.expiresAt) and is single-use.
Empty JSON body {} is accepted; no input schema needed for the token step.
Response includes an img402 metadata block (news/thanks/feedback) that is informational only.
Provider also offers permanent hosting for $1 via POST /api/upload/token/permanent.
usage.guide: To host an image with img402, first POST to https://img402.dev/api/upload/token with an empty JSON body {} — this is an x402 paid call ($0.01 USDC on Base) that returns body.token and body.expiresAt. The token is single-use and valid ~10 minutes. Then upload the actual image bytes in a follow-up request, passing the token as the X-Upload-Token header, to receive the permanent/CDN URL, image id, contentType, and sizeBytes. Read body.token from this endpoint's response; do not expect a CDN URL from this step.
